note: Compiled by tools/geography/build-people.mjs from country-people.json. Peoples and traditions, and figures from history named as history.

items.name: Aboriginal Australians
items.note: The oldest continuing cultures on Earth, here for 60,000 years.

items.name: Agojie
items.note: The women soldiers of the kingdom of Dahomey.

items.name: Alexander the Great
items.note: Born at Pella; by thirty he had ridden as far as India.

items.name: Amazigh
items.note: The people of the Atlas, whose name means 'free people'.

items.name: Ancient Greek
items.note: Philosophers, playwrights and the first Olympians.

items.name: Apsara dancer
items.note: The dancers carved on the walls of Angkor, still dancing.

items.name: Asante
items.note: The kingdom of the Golden Stool, and of kente cloth.

items.name: Aztec
items.note: A city built on a lake, with floating gardens for fields.

items.name: Balinese dancer
items.note: Every finger and every eye moves, and none of it by accident.

items.name: Basotho horseman
items.note: A pony, a blanket and a mountain path — how you travel here.

items.name: Bedouin
items.note: Black goat-hair tents pitched among the red rocks of Wadi Rum.

items.name: Csikós
items.note: Horsemen of the puszta, who ride standing on two horses at once.

items.name: Dogon
items.note: Cliff dwellers of Bandiagara, with masks as tall as a house.

items.name: Eagle hunter
items.note: A golden eagle on the arm, trained to hunt across the steppe.

items.name: Fado singer
items.note: Songs about missing something you cannot quite name.

items.name: Genghis Khan
items.note: From one camp on the steppe to the largest land empire there has been.

items.name: Guna
items.note: Molas: layer on layer of cloth cut away to make a picture.

items.name: Haenyeo
items.note: The sea women of Jeju, who dive without air tanks, well into old age.

items.name: Highland piper
items.note: Bagpipes that can be heard from the far side of a glen.

items.name: Himba
items.note: Cattle herders of the far north, in red ochre and braids.

items.name: Huli wigman
items.note: Wigs grown from their own hair and decorated with everlasting daisies.

items.name: ʻŌteʻa dancer
items.note: Drums so fast the hips can barely keep up.

items.name: Ifugao
items.note: Rice terraces cut into the mountain two thousand years ago.

items.name: Inca
items.note: Builders of Cusco and of roads over the whole Andes.

items.name: Inle leg-rower
items.note: Fishermen who row standing up, with one leg wrapped round the oar.

items.name: Inuit
items.note: People of the Arctic, at home where the sea freezes.

items.name: Irish dancer
items.note: Feet like lightning, arms perfectly still.

items.name: Joan of Arc
items.note: A farm girl of seventeen who led an army and lifted a siege.

items.name: Kalash
items.note: Three valleys, their own gods, and festivals full of flowers.

items.name: Kayapó
items.note: People of the Xingu, with headdresses like a yellow sunburst.

items.name: Maasai
items.note: Herders of the Rift Valley, known for their red shukas.

items.name: Māori
items.note: The first people of Aotearoa, who navigated here by stars and swell.

items.name: Mapuche
items.note: The people of the land, who were never conquered by Spain.

items.name: Maroon
items.note: Free towns in the mountains, and an abeng horn to call between them.

items.name: Maya
items.note: Builders of cities and astronomers — and still here, millions strong.

items.name: Mongol horseman
items.note: Riders of the steppe, who once crossed a continent on horseback.

items.name: Naghol land diver
items.note: A tower of sticks, two vines round the ankles, and a dive.

items.name: Native American peoples
items.note: The many nations who lived here long before anybody sailed in.

items.name: Pharaoh
items.note: The rulers of ancient Egypt, buried under mountains of stone.

items.name: Phoenician sailor
items.note: Traders who sailed the whole Mediterranean and gave us the alphabet.

items.name: Pirate
items.note: For a few years Nassau was run by pirates and nobody else.

items.name: Polar explorer
items.note: Wooden huts, sledges and dogs — and a race for the South Pole.

items.name: Quechua
items.note: Speakers of the language of the Inca, farming the high Andes.

items.name: Roman legionary
items.note: The soldiers of an empire that reached from Britain to Egypt.

items.name: Samurai
items.note: Warriors who served Japan's lords for seven hundred years.

items.name: San
items.note: Trackers of the Kalahari, who can read a day-old footprint.

items.name: Sherpa
items.note: People of the high valleys, at home where the air is thin.

items.name: Silk Road merchant
items.note: Samarkand: where the caravans from China met the ones from Rome.

items.name: Steelpan player
items.note: An oil drum beaten into the only new instrument of the last century.

items.name: Viking
items.note: Seafarers and traders of the Norse world, a thousand years ago.

items.name: Water puppeteer
items.note: Puppets danced on a flooded rice field, the poles hidden below.

items.name: Whirling dervish
items.note: One hand up, one hand down, turning for an hour without stopping.

items.name: Wodaabe
items.note: Herders whose young men dance a beauty contest at Gerewol.

items.name: Yoruba
items.note: People of Ile-Ife, of talking drums and bronze heads.

items.name: Zaporozhian Cossack
items.note: A free camp of riders on an island in the Dnipro.

items.name: Zulu
items.note: People of the shield and the beaded message, in KwaZulu.

items.name: Afar
items.note: Herders of one of the hottest places on Earth.

items.name: Aka
items.note: Forest people whose singing weaves many voices at once.

items.name: Akhal-Teke rider
items.note: Desert horses with coats that shine like metal.

items.name: Alphorn player
items.note: A horn as long as three people, once used to call across valleys.

items.name: Amis
items.note: The largest of the island's first peoples, and their harvest songs.

items.name: Aymara
items.note: People of the high plateau around Lake Titicaca.

items.name: Baul singer
items.note: Wandering minstrels who own almost nothing but their songs.

items.name: Beqa firewalker
items.note: One island's families walk barefoot over white-hot stones.

items.name: Bodu beru drummer
items.note: A big drum, a circle of singers, and a dance that speeds up and up.

items.name: Boyero
items.note: Oxcarts painted like flowers, each one with its own creak.

items.name: Breton
items.note: A Celtic corner of France, with bagpipes and a language of its own.

items.name: Buzkashi rider
items.note: A game of horsemen, played across a whole field with no ball.

items.name: Candombe drummer
items.note: Three drums of three different sizes, walking down the street together.

items.name: Celt
items.note: Iron-age people of spirals, torcs and hilltop kings.

items.name: Cham dancer
items.note: Masked dances that whirl in the courtyard of a mountain fortress.

items.name: CHamoru
items.note: The first people of the Marianas, and the fastest sailing canoes in the world.

items.name: Cowboy
items.note: Riders who drove cattle across the western plains.

items.name: Dinka
items.note: Cattle keepers who name themselves after their favourite ox.

items.name: Falconer
items.note: A hunting bird that sits on your glove and comes back to it.

items.name: Flamenco dancer
items.note: Dance, song and guitar from Andalusia.

items.name: Frankincense harvester
items.note: Cut the bark, wait, and collect the tears the tree makes.

items.name: Frisians
items.note: Their own language, and a skating race past eleven towns in one day.

items.name: Fula
items.note: Herders who move across a dozen countries with their cattle.

items.name: Garifuna
items.note: Caribbean and African together, with drums that talk in threes.

items.name: Gaucho
items.note: Horsemen of the pampas.

items.name: Gille of Binche
items.note: Wax masks, ostrich feathers, and oranges thrown to the crowd.

items.name: Gombey dancer
items.note: Peacock feathers, mirrors, whistles and a snare drum through the streets.

items.name: Górale
items.note: Highlanders of the Tatras, in felt hats and wooden houses.

items.name: Griot
items.note: Keepers of a family's history, who sing it rather than write it.

items.name: Gule Wamkulu dancer
items.note: The great dance of the Chewa, danced by masked spirits.

items.name: Hamar
items.note: Cattle keepers of the Omo valley, in ochre and beads.

items.name: Hmong
items.note: Mountain people whose stitched cloth tells whole stories.

items.name: Iban
items.note: Whole villages under one long roof, on the rivers of Borneo.

items.name: Imraguen
items.note: Fishers who wade into the surf, and fish with the help of dolphins.

items.name: Intore dancer
items.note: The dance of heroes, with grass headdresses that swing like manes.

items.name: Junkanoo dancer
items.note: Costumes of crêpe paper, goatskin drums, and a parade before dawn.

items.name: Kabyle
items.note: Amazigh people of the mountains, with a language of their own.

items.name: Kalinago
items.note: The last territory of the Caribbean's first islanders, and their canoes.

items.name: Kanak
items.note: The first people of these islands, and their tall round houses.

items.name: Kandyan dancer
items.note: Silver headdresses, and drums that answer every step.

items.name: Khevsur
items.note: Mountain villagers who still wore chainmail a century ago.

items.name: Khon dancer
items.note: Masked theatre of monkeys and giants, from an ancient story.

items.name: Kukeri
items.note: Hairy monsters hung with cowbells, chasing winter away.

items.name: Lion dancer
items.note: Two people inside one lion, dancing it up a pole for luck.

items.name: Llanero
items.note: Cattlemen of the flooded plains, who sing to the herd at night.

items.name: Lozi of the Kuomboka
items.note: When the flood comes, the king moves house by barge.

items.name: Makonde carver
items.note: Whole families carved from one piece of blackwood.

items.name: Maroon of the Suriname River
items.note: Villages upriver founded by people who freed themselves.

items.name: Marsh Arab
items.note: Houses of reed on islands of reed, in the marshes of two rivers.

items.name: Mbuti
items.note: Hunters of the Ituri forest, at home under the tallest trees.

items.name: Merengue dancer
items.note: An accordion, a two-headed drum, and feet that never stop.

items.name: Nubian
items.note: People of the Nile with pyramids older than some in Egypt.

items.name: Otavalo weaver
items.note: Weavers and traders whose market is famous across the continent.

items.name: Palmyrene trader
items.note: Caravan merchants of a city of columns in the middle of the desert.

items.name: Pearl diver
items.note: Down on one breath with a stone, up with a basket of oysters.

items.name: Peranakan
items.note: Chinese and Malay together for centuries — in the tiles, the beads and the food.

items.name: Persian carpet weaver
items.note: A garden, drawn in knots, that takes a year to finish.

items.name: Royal drummer of Burundi
items.note: Drums carried on the head, played by whole teams at once.

items.name: Sahrawi
items.note: Desert people of the western Sahara, in indigo and tents.

items.name: Sámi
items.note: The indigenous people of the far north, herders of reindeer.

items.name: Séga dancer
items.note: Feet sliding on sand — in this dance they never leave the ground.

items.name: Shona stone carver
items.note: Builders of Great Zimbabwe, and carvers of its birds.

items.name: Soldier of the Haitian Revolution
items.note: The enslaved rose, won, and made the first free Black republic.

items.name: Somali camel herder
items.note: More camels here than almost anywhere on Earth.

items.name: Son musician
items.note: A tres guitar, a bongo and a chorus, on a porch in Santiago.

items.name: Stick chart navigator
items.note: A map of sticks and shells that shows where the waves bend.

items.name: Swazi reed dancer
items.note: Thousands dance to the royal village carrying cut reeds.

items.name: Swiss Guard
items.note: Striped uniforms and a halberd, guarding the smallest country there is.

items.name: Tatreez embroiderer
items.note: Cross-stitch in red thread, where every village has its own pattern.

items.name: Terracotta warrior
items.note: An army of clay, buried to guard an emperor.

items.name: Tuareg
items.note: The blue-veiled people of the Sahara, who cross it by camel.

items.name: Tufuga tā tatau
items.note: Tattoo masters who work with a comb of bone and a mallet.

items.name: Vejigante
items.note: A carnival demon in a horned mask made of papier-mâché.

items.name: Vezo
items.note: Fishing people of the west coast, who sail outrigger canoes.

items.name: Wayuu
items.note: Desert people of La Guajira, and bags crocheted with their own signs.

items.name: Wolof
items.note: People of the sabar drum, played with a hand and a stick.

items.name: Yapese stone money carrier
items.note: Money the size of a door, which stays put when it changes owner.

items.name: Åland windjammer sailor
items.note: The last great sailing ships in the world worked from here.

items.name: Alpine cowherd
items.note: In autumn the cows come down wearing flowers and enormous bells.

items.name: Ashik
items.note: A travelling singer who carries the news and the old stories.

items.name: Baganda
items.note: People of the kingdom of Buganda, on the shore of the great lake.

items.name: Bamileke
items.note: People of the grassfields, known for beaded masks and elephant dancers.

items.name: Batammariba
items.note: Builders of clay tower-houses that look like little castles.

items.name: Bijagó
items.note: Islanders of eighty islands, with dances that become animals.

items.name: Bohemian glassblower
items.note: Glass gathered on a pipe, and blown while it is still glowing.

items.name: Bounty descendant
items.note: Families descended from the mutineers, with a language of their own.

items.name: Bubi
items.note: The first people of the island of Bioko.

items.name: Carolinian canoe sailor
items.note: Open ocean crossed by the stars, with no instrument at all.

items.name: Chagossian
items.note: Islanders of the Chagos, who fished these lagoons for generations.

items.name: Cossack
items.note: Horsemen of the southern steppe.

items.name: Dhow builder
items.note: Ships sewn and pegged together, built by eye without a plan.

items.name: Fang
items.note: Carvers of guardian figures that watch over the ancestors.

items.name: Faroese chain dancer
items.note: Everyone holds hands in a ring and sings the story as they step.

items.name: Fujara player
items.note: A shepherd's flute taller than the shepherd.

items.name: Geisha
items.note: Artists of dance, music and conversation, trained for years.

items.name: Grand Mariage dancer
items.note: A wedding that lasts days and makes a man an elder.

items.name: Güegüense dancer
items.note: A four-hundred-year-old play where the trickster wins by talking.

items.name: Iso-polyphony singer
items.note: Four voices, one of them holding a single note underneath.

items.name: Kampong Ayer boatman
items.note: A whole town on stilts above the river, older than the cars.

items.name: Khachkar carver
items.note: Cross-stones cut in lace, no two of them the same.

items.name: Kihnu islander
items.note: On this island the women kept the old songs, and the motorbikes.

items.name: Kiribati dancer
items.note: Arms held out and still, like a frigatebird riding the wind.

items.name: Klapa singer
items.note: Men in a stone alley, singing with no instruments at all.

items.name: Klezmer musician
items.note: A clarinet that laughs and cries in the same tune.

items.name: Kongo
items.note: People of an old kingdom on both banks of the great river.

items.name: Kurent
items.note: A shaggy sheepskin monster with a long red tongue, ringing bells at winter.

items.name: Lakalaka dancer
items.note: A whole village in a line, dancing a poem with their hands.

items.name: Lefkara lace maker
items.note: A needle, white thread, and a pattern learned from a grandmother.

items.name: Lenca potter
items.note: Black-and-white pots, coiled by hand and fired in a garden.

items.name: Luzzu fisherman
items.note: Boats painted with an eye on the bow, to watch the sea for you.

items.name: Mahout
items.note: Keepers who live and work alongside elephants.

items.name: Makushi
items.note: People of the savanna between the forest and the mountains.

items.name: Manaschi
items.note: Tellers of the Manas: a poem longer than any book, held in the head.

items.name: Maramureș woodcarver
items.note: Gates and churches carved from oak, with spires like needles.

items.name: Matai
items.note: A village chief and speaker, chosen by the family to talk for it.

items.name: Morna singer
items.note: Songs of the sea and of missing home, sung with a guitar.

items.name: Mossi
items.note: Horse riders who built kingdoms on the bend of the Volta.

items.name: Moutya dancer
items.note: A drum warmed over a beach fire, and dancing until it cools.

items.name: Nahua-Pipil
items.note: The old people of these volcanoes, and their Nawat language.

items.name: Ñandutí lace maker
items.note: Lace made in circles — the name means 'spider web'.

items.name: Ovimbundu
items.note: The largest of Angola's peoples, farmers and traders of the high plateau.

items.name: Palauan storyboard carver
items.note: A whole legend carved along one plank of wood.

items.name: Pamiri
items.note: People of the roof of the world, on the highest road there is.

items.name: Rashaida
items.note: Camel herders of the Red Sea coast, in silver and red veils.

items.name: Senufo
items.note: Carvers and mask dancers of the northern savanna.

items.name: Shell money maker
items.note: Shells ground into beads and strung — still used to buy things.

items.name: Socotri
items.note: Islanders who live among trees that grow nowhere else on Earth.

items.name: Sorbs
items.note: A Slavic people in eastern Germany, with painted eggs and their own language.

items.name: South Georgia whaler
items.note: A rusting station in a bay full of penguins and elephant seals.

items.name: Tais weaver
items.note: Cloth woven for welcomes, weddings and goodbyes.

items.name: Tchiloli player
items.note: A street play five hundred years old, performed in masks.

items.name: Toubou
items.note: People of the Tibesti mountains, in the middle of the desert.

items.name: Ura dancer
items.note: Hips that keep the drum's time exactly, and nothing else moving.

items.name: Volendam fisherfolk
items.note: Lace caps, wooden shoes, and a harbour that lost its sea.

items.name: Anguillian boat racer
items.note: The national sport is sailing wooden boats built on the beach.

items.name: Basque and Breton fisherman
items.note: A piece of France off Canada, settled by cod fishermen.

items.name: Catboat builder
items.note: A small boat built for turtling, shaped entirely by eye.

items.name: Cross crafter
items.note: Carved wooden crosses, and a hill with a hundred thousand of them.

items.name: Crossbowman of San Marino
items.note: A shooting contest under the towers, in medieval dress, every year.

items.name: Echternach dancing procession
items.note: A procession that hops its way through the town every spring.

items.name: Falklands shepherd
items.note: More sheep than people, and a long ride between the farms.

items.name: Fatele dancer
items.note: Everyone sings, and the box they drum on is an empty crate.

items.name: Frigatebird keeper
items.note: Wild seabirds tamed to fly out and come home again.

items.name: Galičnik wedding
items.note: Once a year, one wedding for the whole empty mountain village.

items.name: Gondolier
items.note: Rowers who steer Venice's boats standing up.

items.name: Grimaldi knight
items.note: In 1297 a man disguised as a monk took the rock — and never gave it back.

items.name: Gusle player
items.note: One string, a horsehair bow, and a poem that lasts all evening.

items.name: Hiapo maker
items.note: Cloth beaten from bark and painted with fine spidery lines.

items.name: Kalyady mummer
items.note: A goat, a star and a song, going house to house in midwinter.

items.name: Karagöz puppeteer
items.note: Shadow puppets of camel leather, played behind a lit sheet.

items.name: Kerguelen sealer
items.note: Men left for a year on the islands of desolation.

items.name: Kittitian masquerade dancer
items.note: Peacock feathers and ribbons, dancing between Christmas and New Year.

items.name: Korean drum dancer
items.note: A small drum at the waist, played while spinning.

items.name: Kpelle
items.note: Farmers of the forest, with masks that teach as they dance.

items.name: La Rose society
items.note: Half the island is Rose, the other half Marguerite, and each has its feast.

items.name: Landship performer
items.note: A whole navy on dry land, marching and dancing as a ship.

items.name: Lăutar
items.note: Wedding fiddlers who can play for two days without a sheet of music.

items.name: Macanese
items.note: Four hundred years of Portugal and China in one kitchen.

items.name: Mende
items.note: The only place in Africa where women wear the great masks.

items.name: Njeguši highlander
items.note: A village on the black mountain that gave the country its name.

items.name: Pyrenean shepherd
items.note: Up the mountain in summer, down again before the snow.

items.name: Rugova highlander
items.note: Stone villages up a gorge, and a dance with swords.

items.name: Sailor of Nelson's Dockyard
items.note: A harbour hidden in a bay, where whole fleets were repaired.

items.name: Saint Helena flax worker
items.note: Rope made from flax on the loneliest island in the Atlantic.

items.name: Sevdah singer
items.note: Slow songs of longing, sung in a room too small for them.

items.name: Shortknee masquerader
items.note: Wire masks and powder thrown at carnival, in trousers cut short.

items.name: Suiti
items.note: A small community whose women improvise songs on the spot.

items.name: Tambú drummer
items.note: A drum, a hoe blade for a bell, and songs that say what cannot be said.

items.name: Wallisian dancer
items.note: Dances for the king, in mats and scented oil.

items.name: Cocos Malay
items.note: Islanders of a ring of coral, halfway to nowhere.

items.name: Dande singer
items.note: At New Year a band goes house to house and sings your luck for you.

items.name: Guernsey knitter
items.note: The fisherman's jumper is named after this island.

items.name: Jersey oysterman
items.note: The tide goes out so far here that the island nearly doubles.

items.name: Manx Gaelic singer
items.note: A language that nearly disappeared, and is being sung back.

items.name: Montserrat masquerader
items.note: Irish and African at once, on an island with shamrocks and a volcano.

items.name: Ponum dancer
items.note: A dance that began as a celebration of emancipation.

items.name: Quadrille dancer
items.note: A European square dance, taken over and given a new rhythm.

items.name: Ripsaw musician
items.note: The rhythm is a knife scraped along a carpenter's handsaw.

items.name: Rote fisherman
items.note: Sailors from Rote have fished these reefs for three hundred years.

items.name: Saint-Barth straw weaver
items.note: Hats and baskets plaited from latania palm, and Norman bonnets.

items.name: Saint-Martin salt raker
items.note: Salt raked from the ponds by hand and carried out in baskets.

items.name: Tortola sloop sailor
items.note: Wooden sloops built on the beach and raced between the islands.
